//: Story Phase 2, chapter 7: The Fate of the Treasure. Ruined inspectables live in data/maps/ship/treasure_hold.json (tag ruined_treasure); Penhallow is chained in the crew quarters (10,14).

ch7.begin.narrate: An hour later, the sea wind has carried the worst of the cloud away.
Below decks it has thinned to a sour yellow haze. The crew can breathe again. Mostly.

ch7.nudge: hale[concerned]: Captain. The hold's breathable again. More or less.
hale: Somebody ought to go and look at the treasure.
ch7.reveal: The room is very still. The gold is all still here. Every coin and crown, exactly where it was.
It's just that all of it is... wrong.
captain[devastated]: Somehow that makes it worse.
captain[devastated]: Twelve years. Every raid, every chase, every night I didn't sleep. It's all in this room.
captain[resigned]: Let's see how bad it is.

ch7.reveal.tutorial: Inspect the ruined treasure to see what the Gust has done to it.
ch7.reveal.title: The Price of Gold

ch7.ruined_coin: You pick up a doubloon. It's warm. It shouldn't be warm.
Out of long habit, you bite it.
captain[disgusted]: Blegh! It tastes the way the room smells!
ch7.ruined_ruby: The great ruby of the Viceroy's Hand. Once the size of a hen's egg and the colour of a sunset.
It has gone cloudy. And it smells, unmistakably, of pickled onion.
captain[devastated]: I fought three marines and a governor's wife for that ruby. It's a PICKLED ONION now.
ch7.ruined_crown: The crown of the Isle of Marrow, on its velvet cushion. It has a greasy film, like soup gone cold.
When you lift it, the cushion comes with it.
captain[disgusted]: ...Put it down. Put it DOWN.
ch7.ruined_pearls: A silver bowl of pearls, each the size of a thumbnail. They've turned the yellow of old teeth.
ch7.ruined_chest: The chest Garrick landed on, split down the middle. A thin curl of yellow still breathes out of the crack.
Every coin inside is fused to the next in a yellow crust. It comes out in one piece, like a cake.
ch7.ruined_wall: The planks themselves have taken the stain. You scrape at it with a thumbnail.
It isn't on the wood. It's IN the wood.
ch7.ruined_statue: The little golden sea-captain with the enormous spyglass... appears to be holding his nose.
You're almost certain he wasn't doing that this morning.
ch7.ruined_mirror: The gilded looking-glass has fogged over from the inside.
Your reflection looks exactly the way you feel.
ch7.worth: captain[determined]: ...No. Gold's still gold. Somebody will take it. Somebody always takes gold.
captain: Penhallow. He's a merchant. He'll know what it's worth.
You scoop a handful of the least-sweaty coins into a small chest and tuck it under your arm.
ch7.merchant_test: captain: Penhallow. You're a merchant.
penhallow[annoyed]: Cloth and fine goods. Why? What's that under your arm?
captain: Gold. I'm selling. Name your price.
penhallow[coughing]: *hack* GOOD LORD. Close it! CLOSE IT!
captain: A thousand in gold. For a hundred.
penhallow[disgusted]: No.
captain: Fifty.
penhallow: No.
captain: Ten!
penhallow: No.
captain[alarmed]: One copper! For the lot!
penhallow: No.
captain[devastated]: I'll PAY you to take one coin!
penhallow[offended]: Captain, I am a ransom prisoner, chained to a pillar, who has not bathed in nine days.
penhallow[disgusted]: And I would not take one coin of that. Not one. I would rather be ransomed for the chain.
penhallow: Try spending that in any port on the Sapphire Sea, and they'll burn the shop you spent it in. Then they'll burn you.
captain[devastated]: So it's... worthless?
penhallow: It's worse than worthless, Captain. It's a liability.
captain[devastated]: The Viceroy's ruby. The Marrow crown. I nearly drowned for that crown.
captain[resigned]: ...It's just gone.
penhallow: ...For what it's worth, Captain, I'm sorry. Truly. It's a terrible thing to lose a fortune.
penhallow: Your round friend waddled past a minute ago, by the way. Muttering about 'a second opinion'. He was heading for the hold.
ch7.permanence: garrick[businesslike]: Captain. I've been conducting a professional appraisal.
captain: Will it fade? The smell. Will it wash off?
garrick: That's the thing about a Gust of this calibre, Captain. It doesn't sit ON things.
garrick: With the gold. With the wood. With the ship. It's bonded with the ship, Captain. It's in the grain now.
garrick[pretend]: Very durable paint. The sort they use on lighthouses.
garrick[nervous]: ...How long does paint last, Captain?
captain[resigned]: Get out of my treasure room.
ch7.crew_turns: The crew has Garrick backed against the mainmast. Several of them are holding things with edges.
brask[annoyed]: Word's got round, Captain. About the treasure.
mags[angry]: Twelve years of shares. Gone. Because HE wanted a snack.
jim[angry]: I TOLD you. I told ALL of you.
garrick[terrified]: Captain! A counter-proposal! Mercy, at a very reasonable rate—

then: captain[angry]: Fine. ENOUGH! All of you!

ch7.crew_turns: captain[determined]: Nobody goes overboard without a trial. We're pirates, not animals.
quill: We're quite a lot like animals, Captain.
captain[angry]: A TRIAL. At sundown. On this deck. Quill, draw up the charges.
